info.title: Mittwald API (subset)
info.description:
## Introduction

This OpenAPI spec documents the mittwald API. It follows the
[OpenAPI 3.0.0 specification](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.0.0.html).

## Authentication

You will need an API token to access the API. You can obtain one by logging into the
[mStudio](https://studio.mittwald.de) and navigating to the
["API Tokens" section in the user menu](https://studio.mittwald.de/app/profile/api-tokens).

When making requests to the API, you can authenticate by passing your API token in the `X-Access-Token` header or as a
bearer token.

## Rate Limiting

Please note that usage of the API is rate-limited to prevent abuse. You can inspect the rate limiting for your current
user by observing the `X-Ratelimit-*` headers included in each response.

## mStudio

A main consumer of the mittwald API is the management interface for our customers, the
[mStudio](https://studio.mittwald.de).

## Contact and support

For support, please use the [mStudio support area](https://studio.mittwald.de/app/support/conversations) or drop us an
email at [support@mittwald.de](mailto:support@mittwald.de).

For security issues, please report to [security@mittwald.de](mailto:security@mittwald.de).

userInputs.description: Values for template user inputs. Missing optional values are filled from template defaults.

prefix.description: Generated, immutable identifier of the Stack (e.g. `st-XXXXXX`). Managed apps in the same project can resolve a container of this Stack as `<serviceName>.<prefix>`; containers of the same Stack can use the service name alone, and containers of other Stacks cannot communicate with it. The prefix is also the directory of the Stack's service log files (`/var/log/container/<prefix>/` in the project file system).

templateId.description: Id of the Template used to create this stack, if one was used.

command.description: The container command (equivalent to the [Docker cmd](https://docs.docker.com/reference/dockerfile/#cmd)). When omitted, this defaults to the command defined in the image.

description.description: Deprecated by 'x-description' (which takes precedence). This field will be removed in a future version.

entrypoint.description: The container entrypoint (equivalent to the [Docker entrypoint](https://docs.docker.com/reference/dockerfile/#entrypoint)). When omitted, this defaults to the entrypoint defined in the image.

environment.description: Key-value map of environment variables that should be passed into the container.

envs.description: DEPRECATED: Use 'environment' instead. This field will be removed in a future version.

image.description: The image to run, in the usual format also used by `docker run` and `docker compose`. The image must exist and be accessible when the request is made, because its digest (and, for a new Service, the user it runs as) is resolved at that time; otherwise the request is rejected. Changing the image of an existing Service keeps the user that was resolved when the Service was created. For an image from a private registry, create a Registry with matching credentials first (`POST /v2/projects/{projectId}/registries`); the Registry is matched by the registry host of the image reference.

ports.description: Ports exposed by this container. Each item has the format `<port>[/<protocol>]` or `<port>:<port>[/<protocol>]`, where `<port>` is a single port or a range such as `8000-8010`. When both sides are given, they must be identical; mapping a port to a different number is not supported. `<protocol>` is `tcp` (default), `udp` or `sctp`. Exposed ports can be accessed from containers of the same Stack and from managed apps in the same project, but not from containers of other Stacks, and are not publicly reachable; to expose a port publicly, connect it with an ingress resource. A service may expose at most 200 port entries, and a port range may span at most 800 ports.

restart.description: Restart policy for the container, using the values of the [Docker Compose `restart` field](https://docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/services/#restart): `no`, `always`, `on-failure` or `unless-stopped`. `unless-stopped` currently behaves like `on-failure`, a maximum retry count (`on-failure:<max-retries>`) is accepted but ignored, and unrecognized values are treated as `on-failure`. Defaults to `on-failure`, so omitting it resets the restart policy of an existing service to `on-failure`.

restartPolicy.description: Deprecated by 'restart' (which takes precedence). This field will be removed in a future version.

volumes.description: Volume mounts for this container. Each item has the format `<source>:<target>`; access-mode suffixes such as `:ro` are not supported. `<target>` is an absolute path inside the container. `<source>` is either the name of a Volume of this Stack (declared in the same request or already existing), or an absolute path in the (always present) project file system, which is shared among containers and managed apps within a project. Mounting the root of the project file system (`/`) is not supported.

Changing the image of an existing Service keeps the user that was resolved when the Service was created. For an image from a private registry, create a Registry with matching credentials first (`POST /v2/projects/{projectId}/registries`); the Registry is matched by the registry host of the image reference.

de.mittwald.v1.container.ServiceStatus.description: Status of a Service. `creating`: the Service was declared and has not reported a status yet. `starting`: the container is being started. `running`: the container is ready. `stopping`: the container is being stopped or terminated. `stopped`: the container was stopped or has exited. `error`: the container or its image is in an error state; see the Service's `message` for details. `unspecified`: the cluster currently reports no decisive condition for the container.

path.description: The path to the part of the data that was validated. JavaScript property access notation (e.g., ".prop[1].subProp") is used.

type.description: ajv validation error type (e.g. "format", "required", "type") or own validation error types

context.description:
The object with the additional information about the error that can be used to create custom error messages. Keys depend on the
type that failed validation (e.g. "missingProperty" for type "required")

cpus.description:
CPU limit for the container. The value can be specified as a decimal number, where `1` corresponds to
one full CPU core. For example, `0.5` means that the container is limited to using half of a CPU core.

memory.description: Memory limit for the container, as an integer followed by a unit, similar to the [byte values used by Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/extension/#specifying-byte-values): `b` (bytes), `k` or `kb` (kilobytes), `m` or `mb` (megabytes) and `g` or `gb` (gigabytes). Units must be lowercase and are decimal (`1g` = 1,000,000,000 bytes). A number without a unit is not accepted.
